To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TGF‐1β enhances expression of pro‐ inflammatory cytokines and metaloproteinase‐1 in rheumatid arthritis and osteoartritis synovial fibrobasts.
TGF‐beta1 is a potent pro-inflammatory cytokine in RA synovial fibrosis.
TGF‐beta 1, a growth factor expressed abundantly in rheumatoid synovioma, enhances the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and metaloproteases in rheumatoid arthritic synoviocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inflammatory effect of the TGF‐β family in rheumatoid synoviocytes.
the inflammatory effects of TGF‐ β1 on synovial fibrosis and the role of TGF‐1 in the pathogenesis of RA.
the inflammatory effect of transforming growth factor (T‐G‐F) beta 1, which is expressed in the rheumatid arthritis (RA) synovium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TGF‐beta is a potent inducer of pro‐inflammation and pro‐destruction in RA, but this effect is specific only for the RA FLS, not for OA FLS and non‐arthritic cells, which may be due to the difference in cytokine receptors and signal transduction.
TGF‐1 has a pro‐inflammatory effect on RA FLS.
TGF‐beta1 is a cytokine that has a dual effect in RA, depending upon the stage of the disease and the cell type involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inflammatory cytokine, TNF‐α, is a key player in RA.
TGF‐ β1 is an important factor in the pathogenesis of RA, and that the effect is mediated through the activation of pro‐inflammation genes and proteins, such as IL‐1, TNF‐α and MMP‐1.
the TGF‐β is an important cytokine in RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inflammatory effects of TGF‐ β1 are mediated by the induction of pro‐inflamma‐ tory cytokine and MMP‐1 expression, which are dependent on NF‐κB and AP‐1 activation in RA FLS.
TGF‐beta1 is an inflammatory cytokine, not an anti‐inflammatory one, and it can synergize with TNF‐alpha to induce inflammation.
TGF‐beta is a pro‐inflammatory molecule, and this is true in RA as well as in non‐arthritics.
